blocks.text: Turn Words into Images

The world of digital art is huge, and you've probably seen a ton of AI-generated images online. But did you know that you can actually learn to create such images yourself? 

Stable Diffusion is a magic engine that turns words into digital art, and you will discover how to command it here. Let's dive in!
What Is Stable Diffusion?
Stable Diffusion is an AI model that turns your ideas into images — no design skills required. You type a description, and it generates a matching visual.

Stable Diffusion can generate images in a wide range of styles. 

From photorealistic portraits to abstract art, from anime-style characters to oil painting landscapes — if you can describe it, Stable Diffusion can create it.
So, in this guide, you'll learn how to:

• Craft prompts that translate your vision precisely
  • Adjust Stable Diffusion modes for different effects
  • Blend artistic styles
And many more!

Moreover, because learning isn't just about theory, you'll get plenty of chances to put your new skills into action throughout the course.

Let's start with navigation.
Navigating Through Stable Diffusion

You can use Stable Diffusion through different tools and platforms. One of the platforms is OpenArt (which uses newer versions such as SDXL). To start creating, click on the "Image" in the left-hand menu, and you'll find your image creation workspace!
In the workspace, you'll see several key areas:

• Two modes: Create Image and Image Variations (the latter lets you create an image from a reference)
  • Model selector: choose OpenArt SDXL
  • Prompt box: where you type your idea — it also includes Prompt from Image, Enhance Prompt, and Clear Prompt options
  • Output settings: control the aspect ratio and number of generations
Let's begin writing your first creative prompt!

blocks.prompt: Fill in the missing parts of this AI art prompt to complete the scene.
blocks.template: A cozy [place] with fairy lights, an open book, and a steaming cup of coffee, rendered [mood] with warm golden hour lighting

blocks.text: Cool, right? But that's just the beginning. How about something more fantastical?

blocks.prompt: Fill in the missing detail to complete this AI image prompt.
blocks.template: Magical [creature] wearing spectacles, surrounded by floating books in [setting], digital painting with soft volumetric lighting

blocks.text: See how a few well-chosen words shape something entirely different each time? Every detail you add — creature, setting, mood — shifts what the AI creates. That's what prompt crafting is: directing the AI like an artist directing a scene.
In the following lessons, you'll learn even more:

• Defining subject and medium
  • Controlling the color schemes and lighting
  • Image-to-image techniques
As a result, from photorealistic portraits to surreal landscapes, by the end of this course, you'll generate the art you envision.

The Art of Prompt Crafting

Prompts are the way you communicate with AI, and learning how to craft them well will allow you to create images exactly as you imagine.

Therefore, let's dive in and master this art!
Why Prompts Matter

A well-crafted prompt is like a detailed blueprint for a building. 

The clearer your instructions, the closer the final image will be to your vision.

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! Detailed prompts provide more specific guidance to the AI, enabling it to generate images that better match your vision. This precision is key to getting the results you want.

feedbackIncorrect.text: While detailed prompts offer many benefits, they don't necessarily speed up generation or guarantee better quality. Their main advantage is in providing clear, specific instructions to the AI.

options.label: It gives the AI more precise instructions
It always produces better quality images and takes less time to generate

blocks.question: What do you think is the main advantage of using a detailed prompt over a simple one?

blocks.text: To understand the importance of a good prompt, imagine you want to generate an image of a Persian cat. In such a scenario:

• Basically asking for "a cat" will result in any random cat image.
  • In turn, prompting "a regal Persian cat with sapphire eyes lounging on a velvet cushion" will create an exact result that you imagined.
The more precise you are, the better the result will be.
Anatomy of an Effective Prompt
Let's break down the structure of a great prompt. It typically includes:

1. Subject: What's the main focus?
  2. Action or State: What is it doing?
  3. Setting: Where is it?
  4. Style: How should it look artistically?
  5. Mood: What's the overall feeling?

blocks.prompt: Complete the prompt by identifying the key elements: subject, action, setting, and style.
blocks.template: A curious [subject] [action] over a fallen log in [setting], painted [style], with a sense of wonder and adventure

blocks.text: Descriptive Elements

Adjectives bring your prompts to life. They add specificity, color, and emotion to your instructions. Instead of vague or generic results, adjectives help guide AI to generate more vivid, accurate, and engaging outputs.
From the above example, you may have noticed the stylistic specification in the prompt. That is, it asked for an image to be "in the style of impressionism."
The thing is that such artistic terms elevate your prompts even further. Words like "chiaroscuro," "impressionist," or "art nouveau" influence the style of your generated image.

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! The fact that adjectives help doesn't mean that you should use them as much as possible. The real key is thoughtful detail — specific subjects, clear settings, and intentional style choices create the most vivid results.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Not quite. Piling on too many adjectives can actually clutter your prompt. Focus on meaningful details rather than maximum adjectives.

options.label: Maximize the use of adjectives
Add detailed descriptions

blocks.text:
So, when crafting prompts, avoid these mistakes:
  • Being too vague: "A nice landscape" doesn't give the AI much to work with.
  • Overloading: Cramming too many conflicting ideas into one prompt can confuse the AI.
  • Ignoring composition: Remember to specify the focus and arrangement of elements.
  • Neglecting style: Without style guidance, you might end up with a photo when you want a painting.
  • Forgetting mood: The emotional tone can make or break an image.

blocks.text: Practice Makes Perfect

The more you practice crafting prompts, the better you'll get. 

Start simple and gradually add more details. Pay attention to how your choice of words influences the outcome.

Once you master the basics, start experimenting and stay open to unexpected but creative results. In these terms, keeping a prompt journal can help. Note down which words work well and which don't. This way, you'll eventually develop your own style of prompt crafting!

Your First Steps in Image Generation

You've learned how to craft prompts. Now let's look under the hood!

In this lesson, you'll discover how a few key settings can make your images sharper, more accurate, or more creative.
Crafting Your First Prompt
Let's start with a simple prompt and build from there.

blocks.text: Now, let's enhance our prompt by adding a stylistic element, as you did previously. This will make it more specific.

blocks.text: Style is just one lever you can pull. The model you choose — and the reference images you bring in — can shift your results just as much. Let's look at both.
Choosing Your Model

So far, you've been working with OpenArt SDXL — the default model. But OpenArt gives you access to other Stable Diffusion versions, each with its own strengths. Choosing the right model is one of the quickest ways to steer your results before you even write a word.
Stable Diffusion Versions

• OpenArt SDXL — the versatile baseline. A solid starting point for most image types.
  • Juggernaut XL — built on SDXL with a focus on strong realism and fine detail. Best for portraits, product-style images, and anything where accuracy and texture matter.
  • DynaVision XL — a stylized all-in-one 3D checkpoint. Best for illustrated, rendered, or non-photorealistic results with a polished, cinematic feel.

If your prompt is realistic in nature — a person, a place, an object — try Juggernaut XL. If you're going for something illustrated or stylized, DynaVision XL is your starting point. If you want to explore your options first and create a draft to iterate on later, go for OpenArt SDXL.

feedbackCorrect.text: Juggernaut XL is the right call here. It's built for realism and fine detail — exactly what a photorealistic portrait needs. OpenArt SDXL would produce a decent result, but Juggernaut XL gets you closer to the vision with less effort.

feedbackIncorrect.text: DynaVision XL is optimized for stylized and illustrated output — the opposite of what a photorealistic portrait calls for. When accuracy and texture matter, Juggernaut XL is the better fit.

blocks.text: Prompt From Image

You now know how to pick the model that fits your vision. But what if the vision itself is hard to put into words? That's a different kind of stuck. OpenArt has a feature for it: Prompt from Image in the prompt box.
Instead of writing a prompt from scratch, you upload a reference image and Stable Diffusion generates a text prompt that describes it — which you can then use or edit to create something similar.
This is how to use it:

1. In the prompt box, click "Prompt from Image"
  2. Click "Upload" and select an image from your device
  3. Stable Diffusion will generate a prompt describing the image
  4. Use that prompt as-is, or tweak it to steer the result in your direction

This is your prompt: "Textured image of a man in a red vest and glasses writing at a desk. Walls are completely covered in overlapping papers and notes. Warm, focused light from a blue desk lamp illuminates his workspace. Expressive linework, cross-hatching, post-impressionist style, earthy tones, moody atmosphere." It's also a great starting point for experimentation. Try swapping out individual elements — the subject, the lighting, the mood — and see how the image shifts.

blocks.prompt: Swap the elements to create a different version of this image.
blocks.template: Textured image of [subject] in a red vest and glasses writing at a desk. Walls are completely covered in overlapping papers and notes. [Lighting] illuminates the workspace. [Detail], [atmosphere].
tokens: Bold cartoon linework, flat bright colors, comic style

blocks.text: Swapping elements in a prompt gives you creative control. But there's another kind of control that works in the opposite direction — not adding what you want, but removing what you don't.
Negative Prompts

Negative prompts help you exclude unwanted elements, styles, or colors from your image.

Some of the most commonly used negative prompt terms in Stable Diffusion are:

• blurry, low quality — to avoid soft or degraded outputs
  • extra limbs, deformed hands — to reduce anatomical errors in portraits
  • neon colors, oversaturated — to keep color palettes controlled

Samplers and Combined Prompt Techniques

Building on your understanding of the Stable Diffusion features, we'll now explore how to use samplers. We'll also learn how to combine these elements to create more refined and targeted images. This lesson will enhance your ability to control and customize your image-generation process. Let's jump in!
Understanding Samplers

A well-crafted prompt gets you started. But once you move past basic use, you'll notice that two people can write the same prompt and get noticeably different results — because the settings underneath shape the output just as much as the words above. One of the most impactful of those settings is the sampler.
Samplers control how those steps are taken:

• How quickly the image changes
  • How carefully the details are added
  • How smooth or sharp the final result looks
So, once specified in the prompt, different samplers produce different results.
Think of it like drawing a picture by hand:

• One person sketches fast and fixes details later
  • Another draws slowly and carefully from the start
Both can finish a good drawing — they just get there in different ways.
"DPM++" Sampler

Let's go through the most relevant samplers one by one, starting with the "DPM++" sampler. This one is the modern default for most Stable Diffusion models. Offers a good balance of stability, detail, and speed.

blocks.prompt: Generate an image using the "DPM++" sampler to see how it works.
blocks.template: Generate [subject] reading a newspaper using [sampler type]

blocks.text: As you can see, DPM++ produced a clean, balanced result. For most tasks, this is your safest starting point — it handles a wide range of prompts reliably.
Euler

Another sampler is Euler. It's fast and produces more variation between generations. This makes it useful for experimentation — when you're still exploring ideas and want to see different possibilities from the same prompt.

blocks.prompt: Generate the same image using the "Euler" sampler to compare results.
blocks.template: Generate a vintage robot reading a newspaper using [sample type]

blocks.text:
Notice how the result has a slightly different feel? 

Euler introduced more variation in style or textures, which can be helpful when you're experimenting.
Choosing Between Samplers

As you may have noticed, the choice of sampler can affect your results.

Here's a simple guide:

• Use DPM++ as your default
  • Euler when experimenting

blocks.text: Defining the Subject

The subject is the core of your prompt, and more detail leads to a better result. For example, a prompt like "a dog" is too vague. Instead, adding descriptive details like "A golden retriever with a red collar running through a grassy field" gives the AI clear guidance.

blocks.text: The Importance of Specificity

blocks.text: Choosing the Right Medium
The medium you select defines the style of the image. Should it look like a digital painting, a watercolor, or a photograph?
Each medium creates a different look and feel for your image.

• Digital painting: Clean lines and vibrant colors.
  • Oil painting: Bold, textured strokes.
  • Watercolor: Soft, blended tones.

Style can transform a basic concept by giving it the right mood, texture, and artistic vibe. Let's dive into how to apply and experiment with styles in your prompts!
Choosing the Right Style

The style refers to the artistic approach or visual theme of the image. This can range from impressionist to pop art, or even more complex styles like hyperrealistic, fantasy or dark art.

When you use style keywords in your prompt, they guide the AI to generate images with the right artistic flair. Let's take a look at an example.

Take this prompt: "A beautiful and powerful mysterious magician, sitting on a rock, lightning magic, hat, detailed leather clothing with gemstones, dress, castle background, digital art, hyperrealistic, fantasy, dark art." With the addition of "hyperrealistic, fantasy, and dark art," the image becomes more intense, moody, and visually detailed. It now conveys a darker and more mysterious atmosphere.
Next, let's explore some popular styles:

• Realism: Aims to represent subject matter truthfully.
  • Surrealism: Juxtaposes uncommon imagery for dream-like scenes.
  • Pop art: Uses popular imagery from mass media and culture.
You can also reference specific artists or works. "In the style of Picasso's Blue Period" or "reminiscent of Warhol's pop art portraits".

blocks.text: How Style and Medium Differ

You might wonder how Style and Medium are so similar; why do we need them both? 

Here is the trick: while style is about the artistic mood and tone (like pop art, surrealism, or hyperrealism), the medium refers to the method or material used to create the artwork (like digital painting, watercolor, or charcoal). Together, they shape how your image looks and feels, but they serve different purposes.

For example, a digital painting can be made in a hyperrealistic style. A watercolor can be done in a fantasy style.

The medium defines the visual technique, while the style brings the artistic mood.

Beyond Text-Only Prompts

You've mastered crafting prompts with subject, medium, style, color, and lighting.

Now it's time to level up: you'll learn how to use existing images as your foundation, transforming them into something new while maintaining complete control. This is how you create consistent characters and tell visual stories with AI!
What Is Image-to-Image Generation?

Image-to-image generation uses an existing image as a starting point. Instead of creating from scratch, you provide a reference image and guide the AI to transform it — keeping some elements while changing others. This gives you more control and consistency than text-only prompts.

blocks.text: What Have You Learned?
In this lesson, we will review all the key concepts you've mastered so far. Let's see how well you remember the steps to create a visually stunning AI-generated character!
The Challenge
Your task is to create a consistent character and tell their story across three scenes. You'll apply every Unit 2 technique in a single workflow — this is where theory becomes practice.
The Story Begins
Every great story starts with a character. Imagine you need to create an explorer who's about to embark on an adventure to find a legendary artifact hidden deep in ancient ruins.

Your first task is to bring this explorer to life — define who they are, what they wear, and how they look as they set out on this adventure. This opening scene sets the foundation for everything that follows, so make every detail count!

green explorer jacket and leather backpack

blocks.text: Perfect!
Your explorer is ready for adventure! Let's follow them into the heart of their journey as they discover the ancient ruins.
The Journey Continues
Now our explorer has ventured deep into the jungle and found what they've been searching for — mysterious ancient ruins shrouded in mist.

blocks.prompt: Try uploading your character image in "Image Variations" and placing it in a different environment.
blocks.template: The same character from the reference image, now [action] in [location], [medium], [lighting style]

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! Two things created consistency: the reference image gave the AI the exact visual to work from, and your prompt specified "same character" plus matching medium and lighting. This combination ensures recognition across scenes.

feedbackIncorrect.text: The AI doesn't have memory between generations. Consistency came from your reference image and your prompt. You said "the same character" and repeated the medium and lighting details. Without the reference image and matching prompt elements, you'd get a different-looking person.

All characters automatically look consistent across images

blocks.question: Why does this character look the same as the first image?

feedbackCorrect.text: Even with a reference image, you must repeat the medium, lighting, and style in every prompt. The reference provides visual structure, but without matching prompt elements, the AI might change the rendering style, lighting, or overall aesthetic, breaking consistency.

feedbackIncorrect.text: This approach will break consistency. The reference image alone isn't enough. You need to repeat the medium, lighting, and style details in every single prompt. It's like: reference image + matching prompt = consistency. Remove either part, and you'll get variations.

blocks.question: Create the character once with detailed prompts, then for new scenes, upload the reference image and describe the new background. No need to repeat the style, medium, or lighting in the prompts.

blocks.text: The Grand Finale
Finally, after navigating through the ruins, our explorer has found what they've been searching for — the legendary glowing artifact hidden in an underground chamber. This is the moment of triumph!

blocks.prompt: Complete your character's journey with the climactic discovery.
blocks.template: The same character from the reference image, now [action] with [expression], in [location], [medium], [lighting]

feedbackCorrect.text: Perfect! You kept the character identical with the reference image, repeated medium and lighting in every prompt, and only changed the action and location. That's visual storytelling!

feedbackIncorrect.text: The backgrounds were different — jungle, ruins, chamber. Cohesion came from character and style consistency, not locations. The AI doesn't automatically know you're telling a story. You created that connection by using reference images and matching prompt elements in every scene.

The AI understood it was telling a story and automatically matched the style

blocks.question: Amazing! You've brought your explorer's journey to life from start to finish. Now, what made this three-scene adventure feel like one complete, cohesive story?

blocks.text: Your Story Is Complete!

Nicely done! You've just created a complete visual narrative — from the explorer's confident beginning, through their exciting discovery, to their triumphant moment of success. 

This is the power of combining all covered techniques: consistent character, matching style elements, and purposeful scene progression.

• Same character reference image in every scene
  • Identical medium, lighting, and style repeated
  • Only location and action change to tell the story
